did_you_know.text: Did you know? David mourned Absalom so deeply that he said, “If only I had died instead of you”—he was willing to die in his son’s place.

Did you know? The people’s celebration of victory turned into mourning because they heard that the king was grieving for his son. As a result, the warriors entered the city quietly and ashamed, as though they had fled from battle.
Did you know? Joab rebuked David, saying that his mourning for Absalom made it seem as though he loved his enemies and hated those who loved him—the warriors who had risked their lives for him.

Did you know? After Joab warned David, the king rose and sat at the city gate. His appearance there encouraged the people, and all the warriors came before him. By then, Israel had already fled, each man to his own tent.

Did you know? David offered Amasa, who was his relative, the position of army commander in place of Joab. In this way, David sought to strengthen his relationship with Amasa and change the army’s leadership.
Did you know? Shimei son of Gera, who had cursed David when he fled from Jerusalem, now hurried to ask for forgiveness and was the first from the house of Joseph to come down to meet the king.

Did you know? Although Abishai demanded that Shimei be put to death for cursing “the LORD’s anointed,” David swore that he would not die. David explained that no one should be killed on the day he returned to being king over Israel.

Did you know? Mephibosheth had not cared for his feet, trimmed his mustache, or washed his clothes throughout the entire time David was away from Jerusalem, as a sign of mourning and expectation for the king’s return.
Did you know? Barzillai the Gileadite was eighty years old when he accompanied David to the Jordan, and he was the one who provided for the king while he stayed at Mahanaim.

Did you know? After the Jordan was crossed, an argument broke out between Judah and Israel. Judah claimed a special closeness to the king, while the men of Israel argued that they represented a larger share of the people. The dispute grew more heated, even though everyone wanted to restore David to his kingship.
